Cincinnati

the Queen City — chili, Over-the-Rhine & the Ohio riverfront

109 places · 68 sights · 41 to eat & drink · 7 areas · 18 sources · status last checked 2026-08-18

Downtown & The Banks 22

  1. Must see · Cincinnati Chili · Downtown & The Banks

    Skyline Chili (Downtown)

    The defining Cincinnati-chili brand, founded 1949 by Greek immigrant Nicholas Lambrinides. The downtown parlor is the classic city stop for a cheese coney (mustard, chili, mound of cheddar) and the 4-way onion.

    1001 Vine St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, USA TODAY 10BEST, Wikipedia (published facts/coords), STEFANJOHNSON

  2. Must see · Downtown & The Banks

    21c Museum Hotel Cincinnati

    A free contemporary-art museum threaded through a boutique hotel in the 1912 Neoclassical Hotel Metropole (on the National Register) — rotating exhibitions open to the public 24/7, plus roaming site-specific installations and the signature yellow penguins.

    Your guide’s note Museum is free and open around the clock; docent tours on select days.

    609 Walnut St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  3. Must see · Downtown & The Banks

    John A. Roebling Suspension Bridge

    Opened 1867 as the longest suspension span in the world, John A. Roebling's Ohio River bridge was the prototype for his Brooklyn Bridge; its illuminated cables are Cincinnati's signature riverfront image.

    100 W Mehring Way, Cincinnati, OH 45202 (Covington side: 200 Riverside Dr, Covington, KY 41011)

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  4. Must see · Downtown & The Banks

    Fountain Square & the Tyler Davidson Fountain

    The city's civic living room since 1871, anchored by 'The Genius of Water,' Ferdinand von Miller's bronze fountain gifted by Henry Probasco in memory of Tyler Davidson.

    520 Vine St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  5. Must see · Downtown & The Banks

    National Underground Railroad Freedom Center

    Opened 2004 on the riverfront where escaping slaves crossed the Ohio, this museum tells the story of the Underground Railroad and contemporary freedom struggles, anchored by a rescued slave pen.

    50 E Freedom Way, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  6. Must see · Downtown & The Banks

    Great American Ball Park & Reds Hall of Fame

    Riverfront home of the Cincinnati Reds, baseball's oldest professional franchise, since 2003; the adjoining Reds Hall of Fame & Museum honors the Big Red Machine.

    100 Joe Nuxhall Way, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  7. Must see · Downtown & The Banks

    Taft Museum of Art

    European old masters (Rembrandt, Turner, Hals, Ingres) plus Chinese porcelains and French Renaissance enamels inside an 1820 Federal mansion with Robert S. Duncanson murals; bequeathed to the city in 1927.

    Your guide’s note Historic house museum, small but exceptional; check hours.

    316 Pike St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  8. Must see · Downtown & The Banks

    Contemporary Arts Center

    Zaha Hadid's 2003 Lois & Richard Rosenthal Center — the first American art museum designed by a woman, an internationally studied piece of architecture at 6th & Walnut.

    Your guide’s note Rotating contemporary shows; the building itself is the draw.

    44 E 6th St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  9. Must see · American & New American · Downtown & The Banks

    Boca

    David Falk's flagship in the old Maisonette space — award-winning European cooking with French precision; Cincinnati Magazine's No. 1 Best Restaurant.

    114 E 6th St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  10. Must see · American & New American · Downtown & The Banks

    Sotto

    Candlelit subterranean Italian below Boca — famed short rib cappellacci and truffle-season tajarin; Cincinnati Magazine No. 3 Best Restaurant.

    118 E 6th St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  11. Must see · American & New American · Downtown & The Banks

    Mita's

    Chef Jose Salazar's Spanish/Latin American tapas room named for his Colombian grandmother; Salazar is a James Beard nominee/finalist.

    501 Race St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  12. Must see · Mexican & Latin · Downtown & The Banks

    Nada

    David Falk's upscale modern-Mexican room on the Aronoff plaza — reimagined menu and one of downtown's best patios (confirmed open 2025).

    600 Walnut St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  13. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    Weston Art Gallery

    The Aronoff Center's free, street-level contemporary gallery — Cincinnati's premier showcase for emerging and established local and regional artists across all media.

    Your guide’s note Free admission; open around Aronoff performance hours — check the schedule.

    650 Walnut St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  14. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    Paycor Stadium

    The riverfront home of the NFL's Cincinnati Bengals since 2000 (formerly Paul Brown Stadium), part of the downtown sports-and-Banks corridor.

    1 Paycor Stadium, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  15. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    TQL Stadium

    FC Cincinnati's $250M soccer-specific stadium in the West End, opened 2021, known for a translucent LED-lit facade and one of MLS's loudest atmospheres.

    1501 Central Pkwy, Cincinnati, OH 45214

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  16. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    Smale Riverfront Park & Carol Ann's Carousel

    A landscaped riverfront park between the ballpark and stadium with swings, water features and Carol Ann's Carousel, whose 44 hand-carved animals honor Cincinnati history.

    166 W Mehring Way, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Visit Cincy (official CVB), Cincinnati Magazine

  17. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    Sawyer Point & the Serpentine Wall

    A mile of riverfront park at Yeatman's Cove where the stepped Serpentine Wall (1976) descends to the Ohio, a classic spot to sit and watch the river and the Kentucky skyline.

    705 E Pete Rose Way, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  18. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    The Banks

    An 18-acre mixed-use riverfront district tucked between the ballpark and Paycor Stadium, tying together restaurants, bars and residences alongside Smale Park and the Freedom Center.

    150 E Freedom Way, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  19. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    Cincinnati Fire Museum

    200+ years of firefighting history in the restored 1906 Court Street Firehouse — Cincinnati created the nation's first paid professional fire department in 1853.

    Your guide’s note Housed in a National Register 1906 firehouse; limited hours.

    315 W Court St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  20. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    Isaac M. Wise (Plum Street) Temple

    One of the best-preserved Moorish Revival buildings in the US (1866), a National Historic Landmark tied to Reform Judaism founder Rabbi Isaac Mayer Wise.

    Look for Active synagogue; interior by tour/arrangement.

    720 Plum St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Ohio History Connection / historical markers

  21. Worth the detour · Downtown & The Banks

    Cathedral Basilica of St. Peter in Chains

    Greek Revival 'White Angel' cathedral (1845) at 8th & Plum with a soaring spire and mosaic interior, seat of the Archdiocese of Cincinnati.

    Your guide’s note Active cathedral; open for visits around services.

    325 W 8th St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  22. Closed — kept for the record · Downtown & The Banks

    Carew Tower Observation Deck — CLOSED

    The 49th-floor open-air deck atop the 1931 Art Deco Carew Tower (by the Empire State Building's architects) long gave the best downtown-and-river panorama.

    Your guide’s note Deck closed as of 2026 during the tower's conversion to apartments; slated to reopen but no date announced. The building's ground-floor Art Deco arcade remains accessible.

    441 Vine St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton 13

  1. Must see · German & Goetta · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Eckerlin Meats

    An old-fashioned Findlay Market butcher, family-run since 1852, voted Cincinnati's Best Goetta and selling 400-500 lbs a week — the goetta many city diners (including Tucker's) buy to griddle. Grab a loaf plus the house mettwurst.

    116 W Elder St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), Cincinnati Magazine, WKRC 12

  2. Must see · Asian · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Pho Lang Thang

    Cincinnati's standout Vietnamese kitchen, grown from a Findlay Market stall (2011) to a full Race Street room with a bar. 20-hour broth from Ohio Sakura Farms Wagyu, lemongrass grilled pork, sharp banh mi.

    1828 Race St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, Cincinnati Refined, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  3. Must see · American & New American · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Taste of Belgium

    Began 2007 as a 120-lb cast-iron waffle iron in the back of a Findlay Market produce shop; now the caramelized-sugar Liege waffle and the waffle-and-fried-chicken are a Cincinnati brunch signature.

    1801 Race St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, Visit Cincy (official CVB), Official venue/city/park websites

  4. Must see · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Cincinnati Music Hall

    Samuel Hannaford's 1878 High Victorian Gothic landmark facing Washington Park, home to the Cincinnati Symphony, Pops, Opera and Ballet, reopened in 2017 after a $143M restoration.

    1241 Elm St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  5. Must see · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Findlay Market

    Ohio's oldest continuously operated public market (1855), an iron-framed OTR institution packed with Eckerlin Meats, Pho Lang Thang and dozens of vendors plus a weekend farmers' market.

    1801 Race St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  6. Must see · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Over-the-Rhine Historic District

    One of the largest, most intact urban historic districts in the U.S. (NRHP 1983, ~943 contributing buildings) with the country's largest contiguous collection of 19th-century Italianate architecture, built by German immigrants.

    Vine St & E 12th St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Visit Cincy (official CVB), Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  7. Must see · Ice Cream & Bakeries · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Allez Bakery

    OTR artisan boulangerie whose traditional French sourdough and baguettes earned Food & Wine's 'best bread in Ohio' nod (via CityBeat); pastries and sandwiches too. Open, with a Madisonville sibling.

    1208 Main St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  8. Must see · American & New American · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Pepp & Dolores

    Thunderdome Group's homage to founders' Italian grandparents — pasta made fresh daily; voted Best Italian by CityBeat readers 2025 and a 2026 Yelp Top-100 pick.

    1501 Vine St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  9. Must see · Asian · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Teak OTR

    Longtime Cincinnati Thai favorite reopened across from Washington Park; voted CityBeat's Best Thai 2025.

    1200 Race St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), Cincinnati Magazine

  10. Must see · Breweries & Beer · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Rhinegeist

    The brewery that helped launch OTR's beer revival, in the 1890s Christian Moerlein bottling hall; flagship Truth IPA and a rooftop bar. CityBeat's Best Local Brewery.

    1910 Elm St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  11. Worth the detour · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    American Legacy Tours — Queen City Underground

    The signature walking tour into Over-the-Rhine's pre-Prohibition brewing world — subterranean lagering tunnels, a former crypt and the Gateway saloon district; voted Best Historical Tour by Cincinnati Magazine and a USA Today top-five underground tour.

    Your guide’s note Guided tour; tickets and set departure times — book ahead.

    1332 Vine St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  12. Worth the detour · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Washington Park

    A restored 6-acre park (reopened 2012) across from Music Hall with an interactive fountain, bandstand and event lawn, the green heart of Over-the-Rhine's revival.

    1230 Elm St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  13. Worth the detour · Breweries & Beer · Over-the-Rhine & Pendleton

    Northern Row Brewery & Distillery

    OTR Brewery District brewery-and-distillery in Christian Moerlein's 1895 icehouse — clean lagers and ales (pilsner, amber marzen) plus house-distilled gin, whiskey and bourbon, with a scratch kitchen. CityBeat feature; Cincinnati Magazine bucket list.

    111 W McMicken Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), Cincinnati Magazine

Uptown 5

Clifton, Corryville & CUF

  1. Must see · Uptown

    Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden

    The nation's second-oldest zoo (1875) and an accredited botanical garden, now world-famous as the home of Fiona the hippo, born prematurely in 2017.

    3400 Vine St, Cincinnati, OH 45220

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  2. Must see · Uptown

    William Howard Taft National Historic Site

    NPS-run birthplace and boyhood home of the only man to serve as both US President and Chief Justice, in the Mt. Auburn Historic District.

    Your guide’s note Free NPS site; ranger tours of the restored home.

    2038 Auburn Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45219

    Recommended by National Park Service, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  3. Must see · Pizza · Uptown

    Adriatico's

    UC-campus institution famous for the giant 30-slice 'Bearcat' pizza (serves 10–12). A Cincinnati Magazine Top-25 pizza pick and a stop on Dave Portnoy's viral Nov 2025 Cincinnati pizza tour.

    113 W McMillan St, Cincinnati, OH 45219

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, DAVEPORTNOY

  4. Worth the detour · Uptown

    Burnet Woods

    A 90-acre Clifton green space hugging the University of Cincinnati, with a fishing lake, disc-golf course, historic bandstand and the Trailside Nature Center's Wolff Planetarium — the oldest planetarium west of the Alleghenies.

    Your guide’s note Free; open 6a–10p. Designated an Audubon Important Bird Area.

    3251 Brookline Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45220

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  5. Worth the detour · Uptown

    Bellevue Hill Park

    Clifton Heights hillside park with a grand, wide-open view over the entire Cincinnati basin, downtown skyline and the Ohio River.

    Your guide’s note Free; small neighborhood park (not the NKY Bellevue).

    2191 Ohio Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45219

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

East Side 30

Hyde Park, Oakley, Mt. Lookout

  1. Must see · East Side

    Cincinnati Art Museum

    Encyclopedic collection of 67,000+ works spanning 6,000 years, perched in Eden Park; general admission and parking are always free.

    Your guide’s note Free general admission; closed Mondays (Tue–Sun 11–5, Thu to 8).

    953 Eden Park Dr, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  2. Must see · East Side

    Eden Park & Twin Lakes Overlook

    Cincinnati's grand hilltop park above the river — the Twin Lakes overlook gives one of the best Ohio River views in the city, plus the Presidential Grove of memorial oaks (first planted 1882 for Washington).

    Your guide’s note Free, open daily; overlook is in the NE corner.

    950 Eden Park Dr, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  3. Must see · East Side

    Cincinnati Observatory

    The oldest professional observatory in the US and 'Birthplace of American Astronomy,' with one of the world's oldest working telescopes; on its Mt. Lookout hilltop since 1873.

    Your guide’s note Public viewing nights and tours — check schedule.

    3489 Observatory Pl, Cincinnati, OH 45208

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Atlas Obscura

  4. Must see · East Side

    Mt. Adams & Holy Cross-Immaculata Church

    Hillside artists' neighborhood of steep streets and skyline views; its 1859 Immaculata Church draws 10,000+ pilgrims each Good Friday to 'Pray the Steps' up St. Gregory St.

    Your guide’s note Church is active; the Good Friday steps tradition is the signature draw.

    30 Guido St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  5. Must see · Cincinnati Chili · East Side

    Pleasant Ridge Chili

    A neighborhood parlor run by three generations of the Sideris family since 1964, beloved as much for its award-winning gravy cheese fries as its 2-through-5-way chili and homemade coneys.

    6032 Montgomery Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45213

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  6. Must see · German & Goetta · East Side

    Sugar n' Spice

    A sassy pink diner (since 1941) famous for 'wispy thin' pancakes and crisp-griddled goetta — the German pork-and-oats loaf that is Cincinnati's own breakfast meat.

    4381 Reading Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45229

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  7. Must see · Ribs & Barbecue · East Side

    Eli's BBQ

    A riverside East End smoke shack that turned into a Cincinnati favorite: hickory pulled pork, ribs, all-beef dogs and the cult jalapeno-cheddar grits. Cash-friendly, picnic-table casual.

    3313 Riverside Dr, Cincinnati, OH 45226

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  8. Must see · Ice Cream & Bakeries · East Side

    Graeter's (Hyde Park)

    French-pot ice cream, hand-packed 2.5-gallon batches since 1870, with giant chocolate chunks. Cincinnati Magazine named the black raspberry chip a flavor that 'defines' the city; the Hyde Park scoop shop is the classic stop.

    2704 Erie Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45208

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Cincinnati Magazine

  9. Must see · Ice Cream & Bakeries · East Side

    The BonBonerie

    O'Bryonville patisserie (since 1983) whose signature is the Opera Cream Torte — dark chocolate, white chocolate and vanilla opera cream, a distinctly Cincinnati confection — plus schnecken and whimsical iced cookies.

    2030 Madison Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45208

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  10. Must see · Breweries & Beer · East Side

    MadTree Brewing

    Oakley powerhouse with a 20+ tap taproom, wood-fired pizza and beer garden; repeatedly voted among Cincinnati's best breweries.

    3301 Madison Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45209

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), OHIO MAGAZINE

  11. Must see · Burgers & Diners · East Side

    Zip's Cafe

    Mt. Lookout neighborhood tavern, a near-century old; a perennial CityBeat Best Burger and named Ohio's best burger by Food & Wine.

    1036 Delta Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45208

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  12. Worth the detour · Ice Cream & Bakeries · East Side

    Busken Bakery (Hyde Park)

    A hometown tradition since 1928, best known for the yellow-iced 'smiley' cookie (a Cincinnati billboard icon) and buttery schnecken. The Hyde Park shop is the flagship counter.

    2675 Madison Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45208

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  13. Worth the detour · East Side

    Columbia-Tusculum "Painted Ladies"

    Cincinnati's oldest neighborhood (settled 1788) and its answer to San Francisco: a cluster of vividly painted Victorian 'Painted Ladies' perched above the Ohio around Tusculum & Sachem, in the old German truck-farming pocket once nicknamed Wooden Shoe Hollow.

    Your guide’s note A residential streetscape — admire from the public sidewalk; these are private homes.

    Tusculum Ave & Sachem Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45226

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  14. Worth the detour · East Side

    Elsinore Arch

    A castellated 'castle' gateway at the Eden Park entrance, built 1883 by the Cincinnati Water Works as a valve house and styled after Kronborg (Hamlet's Elsinore) after officials saw a Shakespeare production; on the National Register since 1980.

    1700 Gilbert Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Cincinnati Refined

  15. Worth the detour · East Side

    California Woods Nature Preserve

    A hushed 113-acre old-growth ravine forest along the Ohio in the far east end, laced with hilly, bridge-crossed trails and a nature center — one of the city's wildest in-town hikes.

    Your guide’s note Free; trails dawn–dusk (road can flood when the creek rises).

    5400 Kellogg Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45230

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  16. Worth the detour · East Side

    Otto Armleder Memorial Park

    A 300-acre Great Parks riverside meadow in Linwood along the Little Miami, with paved multi-use trails linking to the Lunken Airfield loop, a big dog park and canoe access — prime flat cycling and birding.

    Your guide’s note Free; open green floodplain — trails connect to the Lunken loop.

    5057 Wooster Pike, Cincinnati, OH 45226

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  17. Worth the detour · East Side

    St. Francis de Sales Church & 'Big Joe' Bell

    A soaring 1879 Gothic Revival church at Madison & Woodburn in East Walnut Hills, home to 'Big Joe' — the largest swinging bell ever cast in the United States (~17.5 tons, cast in Cincinnati in 1895), whose first peal reportedly cracked neighborhood windows.

    Look for Active parish; interior viewable around services.

    1600 Madison Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45206

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Cincinnati Refined

  18. Worth the detour · East Side

    Oakley Square & the 20th Century Theater

    The walkable heart of trendy Oakley — a triangular business district of boutiques, restaurants and Aglamesis Bros. ice cream, anchored by the neon-marqueed 1941 20th Century Theater (National Register), now a concert and events venue.

    Your guide’s note Stroll the square; the theater is event-only — check listings.

    3021 Madison Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45209

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  19. Worth the detour · East Side

    Krohn Conservatory

    Art Deco glasshouse in Eden Park (1933) with rainforest, desert and orchid houses and a beloved annual spring butterfly show.

    Your guide’s note Small admission for special shows; closed Mondays.

    1501 Eden Park Dr, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  20. Worth the detour · East Side

    Ault Park

    224-acre Mt. Lookout park crowned by a 1930 Italian Renaissance pavilion; climb to the overlook for panoramic views across the Little Miami valley.

    Your guide’s note Free; hilltop pavilion is a popular event venue.

    3600 Observatory Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45208

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  21. Worth the detour · East Side

    Alms Park

    Hilltop Mt. Lookout park on Mt. Tusculum with several overlooks taking in the Ohio and Little Miami rivers, the NKY hills and Lunken Airport.

    Look for Free, open daily 6a–10p.

    710 Tusculum Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45226

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  22. Worth the detour · East Side

    Harriet Beecher Stowe House

    Walnut Hills home where the future 'Uncle Tom's Cabin' author lived; now an Ohio History Connection museum on abolition and Cincinnati's Black history, reopened after a $2.5M renovation.

    Look for Limited hours; recently renovated.

    2950 Gilbert Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45206

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Ohio History Connection / historical markers

  23. Worth the detour · East Side

    Rookwood Pottery Building

    The 1892 Tudor-style Mt. Adams pottery works of famed Rookwood Pottery, its old kilns big enough to dine in; now a restaurant/bar with skyline views.

    Your guide’s note Building now a restaurant — exterior/architecture and kiln dining rooms are the draw.

    1077 Celestial St, Cincinnati, OH 45202

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  24. Worth the detour · East Side

    Hyde Park Square

    Cincinnati's most charming shopping square, centered on the classical 1900 Kilgour Fountain and a grassy green, lined with 100+ boutiques and cafes.

    Look for Walkable district; Sunday farmers' market mid-May–Oct.

    2700 Erie Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45208

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  25. Worth the detour · East Side

    Village of Mariemont

    A National Historic Landmark 'garden city' — one of America's first fully planned suburbs, laid out in the 1920s by Mary Emery and John Nolen in Tudor-village style with a central concourse and carillon.

    Your guide’s note Historic village ~10 mi east; stroll the square.

    6907 Wooster Pike, Mariemont, OH 45227

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  26. Worth the detour · Ice Cream & Bakeries · East Side

    Aglamesis Bros

    An Oakley Square parlor barely changed since 1913 — Portuguese marble, Tiffany lamps, hand-laid tile — where the Greek Aglamesis family still makes French-pot ice cream and hand-dipped chocolates.

    3046 Madison Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45209

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  27. Worth the detour · Breweries & Beer · East Side

    Nine Giant Brewing

    Pleasant Ridge brewpub pairing expertly-made house beer with scratch gastropub cooking (burgers, shareable small plates) — a neighborhood favorite reviewed by CityBeat and WCPO. Barrel-aged offerings at its nearby Fermentorium.

    6095 Montgomery Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45213

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  28. Worth the detour · Breweries & Beer · East Side

    Streetside Brewery

    Envelope-pushing brewery in Columbia-Tusculum, Cincinnati's oldest neighborhood, with a dog-friendly patio and the Street Chef Brigade food truck parked out front daily. On Cincinnati Magazine's brewery bucket list.

    4003 Eastern Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45226

    Recommended by WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC), Cincinnati Magazine

  29. Worth the detour · Burgers & Diners · East Side

    The Turf Club (Terry's Turf Club)

    Neon-drenched East End icon (ex-Terry's Turf Club, on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives) reopened under new local owners Jan 2025, still building maximalist burgers.

    4618 Eastern Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45226

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  30. Worth the detour · Pizza · East Side

    Taglio

    Columbia Tusculum pizzeria + bar from the A Tavola owners, serving Detroit- and New York-style pizza; a stop on Dave Portnoy's viral Nov 2025 Cincinnati One Bite pizza tour.

    3531 Columbia Pkwy, Cincinnati, OH 45226

    Recommended by DAVEPORTNOY, FOX19

West Side & Northside 12

  1. Must see · Cincinnati Chili · West Side & Northside

    Camp Washington Chili

    Cincinnati's only James Beard honoree for chili (America's Classic, 2000) — a 24-hour parlor since 1940. Order the 5-way: spaghetti, cinnamon-clove chili, kidney beans, diced onion and a mountain of shredded cheddar; the cheese coneys are the sleeper order.

    3005 Colerain Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45225

    Recommended by JAMES BEARD, Cincinnati Magazine, STEFANJOHNSON

  2. Must see · Pizza · West Side & Northside

    LaRosa's (Boudinot)

    The Cincinnati pizza icon: Buddy LaRosa opened here in 1954 using his Aunt Dena's Sicilian recipe (sweeter provolone-topped pies). The original Westwood parlor is the fan-favorite original.

    2411 Boudinot Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45238

    Recommended by WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC), Cincinnati Refined, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  3. Must see · West Side & Northside

    Cincinnati Museum Center at Union Terminal

    One of the last grand Art Deco railroad terminals (1933), a National Historic Landmark whose half-dome rotunda now houses the History, Natural History & Science, and Children's museums plus an OMNIMAX theater.

    Your guide’s note Multi-museum complex; check which museums/exhibits are open before visiting.

    1301 Western Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45203

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  4. Must see · West Side & Northside

    American Sign Museum

    The nation's largest public sign museum — a glowing indoor streetscape of vintage neon and Americana signage in Camp Washington.

    Look for Closed Mon–Tue (Wed–Sun 10–4).

    1330 Monmouth Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45225

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  5. Must see · West Side & Northside

    Spring Grove Cemetery & Arboretum

    A National Historic Landmark garden cemetery (1844) — 733 acres of lakes, monuments and champion trees, one of the largest cemeteries in the US and a designated arboretum.

    Your guide’s note Free; a working cemetery — be respectful.

    4521 Spring Grove Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45232

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  6. Must see · Breweries & Beer · West Side & Northside

    Urban Artifact

    Northside brewery in the historic St. Patrick's Church that owns Cincinnati's 'Midwest Fruit Tart' sour niche — wild and fruited sours like The Gadget gose — plus a taproom, bar and live-music venue. Cincinnati Magazine covered its milestone anniversary.

    1660 Blue Rock St, Cincinnati, OH 45223

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  7. Worth the detour · West Side & Northside

    Mt. Echo Park

    An 84-acre Price Hill hilltop park with one of the West Side's most dramatic overlooks of downtown, the Ohio River and Kentucky, anchored by a 1928 Italian Renaissance pavilion — a favorite golden-hour perch.

    Look for Free; open daily. Pavilion is reservable.

    251 Mt. Echo Park Dr, Cincinnati, OH 45205

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  8. Worth the detour · West Side & Northside

    Olden View Park (Price Hill Incline)

    A small East Price Hill overlook marking the top of the 1874–1943 Price Hill Incline, with a paved path, benches and a historical marker framing a panorama of the river, downtown and Northern Kentucky.

    Your guide’s note Free; open daily. A viewpoint stop, not a full park.

    2610 W 8th St, Cincinnati, OH 45204

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Ohio History Connection / historical markers

  9. Worth the detour · West Side & Northside

    The Betts House

    Ohio's oldest brick house (1804) and the anchor of the Betts-Longworth Historic District — now a small museum of the built environment in the West End.

    Your guide’s note Very small; check for open days/guided tours.

    416 Clark St, Cincinnati, OH 45203

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  10. Worth the detour · West Side & Northside

    Mt. Airy Forest

    At 1,459 acres Cincinnati's largest park and one of the country's largest urban forests, with miles of trails and a free 120-acre arboretum.

    Your guide’s note Free; huge — pick a trailhead or the arboretum.

    5083 Colerain Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45223

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  11. Worth the detour · West Side & Northside

    Northside (Hamilton Avenue District)

    Cincinnati's most eclectic, creative neighborhood — a two-mile stretch of Hamilton Ave lined with locally-owned restaurants, vintage shops, record stores and music venues amid the Italianate Hoffner Historic District.

    Look for Best explored on foot; nightlife-heavy.

    Hamilton Ave & Hoffner St, Cincinnati, OH 45223

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  12. Worth the detour · Cincinnati Chili · West Side & Northside

    Price Hill Chili

    A West Side family restaurant since 1962 with the Golden Fleece Lounge attached — Cincinnati chili 2-through-5-way, cheese coneys, Greek favorites and big all-day breakfasts.

    4920 Glenway Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45238

    Recommended by Cincinnati Refined, Visit Cincy (official CVB)

Northern Suburbs 10

Blue Ash, Montgomery, Mason

  1. Must see · Northern Suburbs

    Loveland Castle (Chateau Laroche)

    A medieval-style stone castle on the Little Miami River hand-built over decades starting 1927 by WWI vet and Boy Scout leader Harry Andrews — a beloved regional oddity.

    Look for Seasonal/weekend hours; NE-suburb drive to Loveland.

    12075 Shore Dr, Loveland, OH 45140

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Atlas Obscura

  2. Must see · Northern Suburbs

    Kings Island

    Regional icon 24 miles NE in Mason — a 364-acre amusement park with 15+ coasters, an Eiffel Tower replica and the Soak City water park, open since 1972.

    Your guide’s note Seasonal (spring–fall + Halloween/holiday events); paid admission.

    6300 Kings Island Dr, Mason, OH 45040

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  3. Must see · Cincinnati Chili · Northern Suburbs

    Blue Ash Chili

    A 1969 Blue Ash institution twice featured on Guy Fieri's 'Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives' — he called the 5-way something he'd eat every day. Add jalapenos for the house 6-way.

    9525 Kenwood Rd, Blue Ash, OH 45242

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  4. Must see · Breweries & Beer · Northern Suburbs

    HighGrain Brewing

    Silverton's first brewery, in the former municipal building — old-world lagers with a modern twist, a top-notch full kitchen, and a sustainability bent (100% wind-powered, a carbon-neutral beer). CityBeat feature; Cincinnati Magazine bucket list.

    6860 Plainfield Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45236

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), Cincinnati Magazine

  5. Worth the detour · Northern Suburbs

    Sharon Woods & Heritage Village Museum

    A Great Parks lake, gorge trail and gardens in Sharonville wrapped around Heritage Village Museum — a dozen relocated 19th-century Southwest-Ohio buildings staffed by costumed interpreters for a living-history walk.

    Your guide’s note Great Parks vehicle pass required; museum has seasonal/limited hours.

    11500 Lebanon Rd, Sharonville, OH 45241

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Cincinnati Magazine

  6. Worth the detour · Northern Suburbs

    French Park

    A 275-acre wooded estate in Amberley Village — bequeathed by printer Herbert Greer French in 1942 — with a hilltop brick manor, a fossil-rich creek and quiet, hilly hiking trails.

    Your guide’s note Free; the French House is a rentable event venue.

    3012 Section Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45237

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  7. Worth the detour · Northern Suburbs

    Fort Ancient Earthworks & Nature Preserve

    The largest and best-preserved prehistoric hilltop enclosure in North America — 18,000+ feet of Hopewell-built earthen walls above the Little Miami, inscribed in 2023 as part of Ohio's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, with an on-site museum.

    Your guide’s note ~40-min drive to Warren County; Ohio History Connection site with seasonal hours.

    6123 OH-350, Oregonia, OH 45054

    Recommended by Ohio History Connection / historical markers, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  8. Worth the detour · Northern Suburbs

    Cincinnati Nature Center (Rowe Woods)

    1,000+ acres of woodland trails, ponds and a nature center in Milford — a longtime regional favorite for hiking and birding.

    Look for Admission/membership; east-suburb drive.

    4949 Tealtown Rd, Milford, OH 45150

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Official venue/city/park websites

  9. Worth the detour · Breweries & Beer · Northern Suburbs

    Fretboard Brewing

    Music-themed Blue Ash microbrewery with a dozen-plus taps, weekly live music and in-house BBQ — a fixture on Cincinnati Magazine's craft-brewery bucket list.

    5800 Creek Rd, Cincinnati, OH 45242

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, Cincinnati Refined

  10. Closed — kept for the record · Northern Suburbs

    EnterTRAINment Junction — CLOSED

    Once home to the world's largest indoor model-train display (25,000 sq ft, 2+ miles of track) in West Chester.

    Your guide’s note CLOSED — permanently shut January 5, 2025. Listed for reference; do not visit.

    7379 Squire Ct, West Chester, OH 45069

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Cincinnati Refined

Northern Kentucky 17

Covington, Newport, Bellevue

  1. Must see · Northern Kentucky

    Newport Aquarium

    A riverfront aquarium at Newport on the Levee with 20,000+ animals, walk-through acrylic tunnels and a rope 'Shark Bridge' suspended over the sharks.

    1 Aquarium Way, Newport, KY 41071

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  2. Must see · Northern Kentucky

    MainStrasse Village

    A restored 19th-century German neighborhood in Covington with Italianate storefronts, bars and the Carroll Chimes Bell Tower's animated Pied Piper show over the Goose Girl Fountain.

    Main St & W 6th St, Covington, KY 41011

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  3. Must see · Northern Kentucky

    Devou Park City Overlook

    The Drees Pavilion overlook in Covington's 700-acre Devou Park frames the definitive postcard view of the Cincinnati skyline across the Ohio, renovated in 2024.

    1201 Park Dr, Covington, KY 41011

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  4. Must see · Cincinnati Chili · Northern Kentucky

    Dixie Chili

    Northern Kentucky's first chili parlor, founded 1929 by Nicholas Sarakatsannis and still slinging 3-, 4- and 5-ways and coneys into the small hours across the river in Newport.

    733 Monmouth St, Newport, KY 41071

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  5. Must see · German & Goetta · Northern Kentucky

    Wunderbar

    A Covington Westside beer hall built on scratch-ground German sausages — Feuerwurst, currywurst, apple-honey wurst — with schnitzel, giant pretzels with beer cheese and 40+ German/craft taps.

    1132 Lee St, Covington, KY 41011

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), Cincinnati Refined

  6. Must see · Asian · Northern Kentucky

    Oriental Wok

    The Wong family's upscale Cantonese-American institution, open in Ft. Mitchell since 1977 (with a Hyde Park sibling) — a near-50-year Greater Cincinnati staple profiled by Cincinnati Magazine and WCPO. Order the honey chicken or Peking duck.

    317 Buttermilk Pike, Ft. Mitchell, KY 41017

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  7. Must see · Breweries & Beer · Northern Kentucky

    Braxton Brewing

    Covington brewery that anchored 7th Street's revival — flagship Storm cream ale and one of NKY's only rooftop taprooms overlooking the river skyline.

    27 W 7th St, Covington, KY 41011

    Recommended by WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC), CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  8. Must see · American & New American · Northern Kentucky

    Bouquet

    Stephen Williams's pioneering NKY farm-to-table bistro sourcing 50+ local farms; Cincinnati Magazine Best Restaurants (No. 9) with a 130-bottle bourbon list.

    519 Main St, Covington, KY 41011

    Recommended by Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  9. Must see · American & New American · Northern Kentucky

    The Baker's Table

    Dave Willocks's tasting-menu-only Newport flagship — Greater Cincinnati's rarest fine-dining format; Willocks is a 2026 James Beard finalist for Best Chef: Southeast.

    1004 Monmouth St, Newport, KY 41071

    Recommended by CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly), WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC)

  10. Must see · Coffee & Cafés · Northern Kentucky

    Carabello Coffee

    Newport roaster and cafe with a barista 'chef's table' Analog Bar; ranked Kentucky's best independent coffee shop, profits funding coffee-origin philanthropy.

    107 E 9th St, Newport, KY 41071

    Recommended by WCPO 9 (Cincinnati ABC), CityBeat (Cincinnati alt-weekly)

  11. Worth the detour · Northern Kentucky

    Rabbit Hash General Store

    A c.1831 riverfront general store — the best-preserved country store in Kentucky and a National Register hamlet famous for electing a dog as honorary mayor; rebuilt faithfully after a 2016 fire and reopened in 2017.

    Your guide’s note ~40-min drive down the Ohio into Boone County, KY; live music weekends.

    10021 Lower River Rd, Rabbit Hash, KY 41005

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  12. Worth the detour · Northern Kentucky

    Big Bone Lick State Historic Site

    The 'Birthplace of American Vertebrate Paleontology' — Ice Age salt-sulfur bogs that trapped mammoths and mastodons, excavated for Jefferson by William Clark in 1807; today a living bison herd, trails and a free museum, named a National Historic Landmark in 2024.

    Your guide’s note Free museum; ~35-min drive into Boone County, KY.

    3380 Beaver Rd, Union, KY 41091

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, National Park Service

  13. Worth the detour · Northern Kentucky

    World Peace Bell

    Cast in France for the millennium, this 66,000-lb (33-ton) bell was the world's largest free-swinging bell when first rung on Jan 1, 2000, its peal carrying up to 25 miles — the centerpiece of downtown Newport's Millennium Monument.

    Your guide’s note Note: moved into storage in 2024 for adjacent construction; Newport plans to reinstall it at a prominent site — confirm it is on display before making a special trip.

    425 York St, Newport, KY 41071

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published facts/coords), Northern Kentucky Tribune

  14. Worth the detour · Northern Kentucky

    Purple People Bridge

    A 2,670-ft former rail bridge, restored in 2006 as a purple-painted pedestrian-only crossing linking Newport on the Levee to downtown Cincinnati with skyline views.

    1 Levee Way, Newport, KY 41071

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  15. Worth the detour · Northern Kentucky

    BB Riverboats

    Long-running Ohio River sightseeing, lunch and dinner cruises departing the Newport landing on Riverboat Row, across from downtown Cincinnati.

    Your guide’s note Regular sightseeing schedule runs roughly Memorial Day to Labor Day; check dates.

    101 Riverboat Row, Newport, KY 41071

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Visit Cincy (official CVB)

  16. Worth the detour · Northern Kentucky

    Newport on the Levee

    A multi-level riverfront dining and entertainment complex (opened 2001) housing the Newport Aquarium, a food hall, cinema and comedy club, at the foot of the Purple People Bridge.

    1 Levee Way, Newport, KY 41071

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Wikipedia (published facts/coords)

  17. Worth the detour · Northern Kentucky

    Behringer-Crawford Museum

    Northern Kentucky's regional history and natural history museum, set inside Devou Park with skyline views over the river.

    Look for In Devou Park (NKY); closed Mondays.

    1600 Montague Rd, Covington, KY 41011

    Recommended by Official venue/city/park websites, Visit Cincy (official CVB)

68 sights and 41 places to eat across Cincinnati and the Northern Kentucky riverfront, each traceable to the source that named it. The city’s food canon is its own: Cincinnati chili (Skyline, Camp Washington), goetta, Montgomery Inn ribs, Findlay Market, Graeter’s ice cream and the German brewing heritage of Over-the-Rhine.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Cincinnati’s signature strength is a food canon all its own: Cincinnati chili (Skyline, Gold Star, Camp Washington — 3-way, 4-way, 5-way and coneys), goetta, Montgomery Inn ribs, Findlay Market, Graeter’s ice cream, LaRosa’s pizza and the German brewing heritage of Over-the-Rhine, reborn at Rhinegeist and MadTree. Every food card names a specific dish, sourced to the Cincinnati Enquirer, Cincinnati Magazine, CityBeat and James Beard. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, Eater SF, The Infatuation, SF Chronicle, Mercury News, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json (direct map/page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sources were confirmed via search). Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open.
